notes: Play knowledge rewritten as executable actions. Every reference is checked against the generated level data by tools/gen_level_nuance.py.
Frigate is the one level where hesitation actively loses objectives: hostages are killed by their captors on a timer, so the usual patient clearing approach is wrong here.

nuance.claim: Each hostage is held at gunpoint and is executed if the captor is left alive too long, so hostage rooms are entered promptly rather than scouted.
Only the guard actually aiming at the hostage needs to die immediately; the others can be fought afterwards, and wide fire into the room kills the hostage.
Captors are killed with headshots because body shots leave them alive long enough to shoot the hostage they are holding.
Opening a door without stepping through leaves the room's guards unaware; they then come into the corridor one at a time instead of engaging together.
The number of hostages that must survive rises with difficulty, so a run that is acceptable on Agent fails on 00 Agent with the same losses.
nuance.because: Objective 0 exists at every difficulty while the bomb objectives do not, and the guides record a rising survival quota.

nuance.claim: Both bombs are disarmed by equipping the bomb defuser and firing at the charge; shooting them with a weapon does not disarm them.
The two bombs are separate objectives in separate parts of the ship, the bridge and the engine room, so neither is on the way to the other.
nuance.because: Objectives 1 and 2 are distinct records naming different locations.

nuance.claim: The helicopter at the stern is bugged by equipping the tracking bug and firing at it, and it is easy to walk past while chasing hostages.
Hostages are uniformed crew rather than obviously civilian figures, so target identification has to happen before firing in occupied rooms.
